title: Assurance of already being justified is posterior to justification; justifying faith’s act is prior
source_text: XXIII. Praeterea modo descripta fiducia est aliquid posterius justificatione, & quod justificationem jam factam consequitur. Prius enim necesse est aliquem justificatum esse, quam ut vere sibi persuadere queat se jam esse justificatum. Sed fidei justificantis actus proprius atque specificus est aliquid, natura saltem, justificatione prius. Quandoquidem juxta Scripturae doctrinam, & Theologorum communem sententiam, fides est nostrae justificationis conditio, sive instrumentum.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, the confidence just described is something later than justification, and which follows justification already made. For it is necessary that someone first be justified before he can truly persuade himself that he is already justified. But the proper and specific act of justifying faith is something, at least in nature, prior to justification. Seeing that according to Scripture’s doctrine and the common opinion of theologians, faith is the condition or instrument of our justification.
pass_b_english: Persuasion that one is already justified comes after justification itself.
Justifying faith’s proper act is naturally prior, as faith is justification’s instrument.
